Cc: Michael Chen <michael.chen@finnova.com>

Subject: Re: Demo today — a couple of follow-ups on deployment options

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate the clarity on latency and cost tradeoffs. A few items the product and security teams asked me to confirm before we move to an internal approval: 

- Which hosted endpoints we can expect in the sandbox (chat vs completion vs embeddings) and whether they have separate rate ceilings.
- Expected per-minute and per-token rate limits on the hosted sandbox (we will be load testing).
- Quick note on Dedicated vs Private: our legal/security team is flagging data residency and KMS for production — but for the initial evaluation we want to keep everything in Hosted. Any gating criteria we should be aware of that would push us to Dedicated/Private earlier?
- Can you share a short list of what you usually provision for a 2-week hosted pilot (endpoints, keys, sample traffic buckets)?

I'm attaching a short security RQ packet (Finnova_Security_RQs.pdf) — our security contact is security@finnova.com.

Thanks,
Elena
Sr PM, Finnova

On Wed, 14 Mar 2028 at 16:10, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai> wrote:

Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 16:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Demo today — a couple of follow-ups on deployment options

Elena — great to meet you and thanks for sending the packet. Quick recap and proposed next steps below so your teams have something tangible to work from: 

Recap / answers:
- Sandbox endpoints: we can provision the following in the hosted sandbox: /v1/chat (stateful chat), /v1/completions (stateless), /v1/embeddings. We usually provide distinct sandbox keys so you can map traffic and rate limit per endpoint.
- Defaults for the hosted sandbox we provision: 60 requests/minute per key with a 20k tokens/minute aggregate soft cap. We can temporarily raise ceilings for a scheduled load test; request at least 48h notice.
- Production gating for Dedicated/Private: Data residency, KMS/HSM integration, and contractual SLAs typically drive customers to Dedicated or Private. For evaluation most customers stay hosted unless they have regulatory or contractual restrictions up front.
- Typical 2-week hosted pilot package we will provision: 2 sandbox API keys, one staging endpoint, basic dashboard access, token-level cost breakdown, and a shared folder with test prompt sets and a small eval harness.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) We provision the hosted sandbox with endpoints above — can you confirm the names of 2 engineers (for key creation)?
2) Ben will coordinate a short load-test window if you want ceilings temporarily increased.
3) Security to send any specific evidence asks to marissa@redwood.ai (SOC2 artefacts, architecture diagram).
4) Schedule a 30-min ops preflight for next Tues (I can host).

Attachments referenced: Finnova_Security_RQs.pdf (from Elena)

I'll loop in Marissa to start the SOC2 + docs handoff.

- Karthik
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Elena,

Thanks for the packet — quick note from my side on load testing and request patterns: if your traffic is bursty with short high-concurrency bursts (chat UIs with many users), we recommend mapping chat traffic to a dedicated key and adjusting the prefetch/batching settings we discussed. If latency-sensitive single-turn completions are the main path, keep those on a separate key and we'll set a lower per-request timeout to preserve SLOs.

I'll be the point for scheduling the temporary ceiling increase during the load test window — send a proposed time and traffic profile and we'll confirm.

Best,
Ben
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
